headline: SITCON eases to 3: Zyxel GS1900 zero-day still unfixed in practice; WordPress KEV patch due today; cPGuard supply-chain attack

bullets.text: Changed: SITCON eased from 2 to 3 (ELEVATED). The last 7 days scored 0.62x the 90-day average; one KEV addition in 72 hours and 4 critical reports in 48 hours keep it above baseline.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Zyxel fixed a zero-day used to hack nearly 1,000 switches, but Help Net Security and The Hacker News report patched switches remained open to the in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441), allowing root command execution.
Due today, WordPress Core: CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a TOCTOU race condition exploited for RCE, added 2026-11-03 with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.
Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: attackers hijacked cPGuard autoupdate in an OpsShield supply-chain attack to deploy a backdoor and steal data.
Still active, CVE-2024-27834: The Hacker News reports a patched Apple flaw is being exploited to deliver info-stealing malware. CISA KEV added it 2026-11-04, federal due date 2026-11-18.

New breaches: a cyberattack hit a French blood bank site (no blood products compromised, per SecurityWeek) and an attack on Norway's aid agency Norad may have exposed all grants-portal user data. CISA/FBI cooling-system hardening warning still stands.

actions: Treat Zyxel GS1900 switches as exposed even after patching: restrict management access, check for compromise, watch for a new fix.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 today (KEV due 2026-11-06).
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18).
Patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935 (KEV due 2026-11-13) and check for compromise.
cPGuard users: hunt for the backdoor delivered via autoupdate and rotate credentials on affected servers.
Operators of cooling and refrigeration systems: apply the CISA/FBI hardening guidance and remove internet exposure of controllers.
